red_flags: Search antitrust remedies (2025 ruling) impose ongoing compliance/distribution-deal uncertainty
AI capex supercycle is compressing FCF yield to near zero
GOOG.one_line: Dominant search/ads plus Cloud and YouTube, with a deep AI moat (Gemini, TPUs, distribution) few can match.
GOOG.reason: Revenue +24% and margins near 55% with net cash; negative forward-EPS figure looks like a swollen prior-year comp (one-off gains), not organic deceleration. NTM P/E of 20.8x is cheap for this quality and growth.

red_flags: Multiple independent short-seller reports (Culper, Fuzzy Panda, Muddy Waters, CapitalWatch) alleging ad fraud, minors targeting and money-laundering ties; formal investigation and securities class actions pending
One accuser (CapitalWatch) retracted its money-laundering claim and apologized in Feb 2026, but core ad-practice allegations remain unresolved
APP.one_line: AI-driven mobile ad network monetizing app installs; high margins but under sustained short-seller fire.
APP.reason: Revenue +53%, EPS growth +61%, 65% margins and 16.5x NTM P/E are exceptional if allegations don't stick; no restatement or going-concern flag yet, but integrity risk is real and unresolved, so this needs full forensic diligence rather than a pass or a buy.

red_flags: Thin GAAP margin (1.1%) typical of an auto-cycle trough
Customer concentration with OEMs pulling back EV capex (GM/Ford)
APTV.one_line: Auto electrical/electronics and software architecture supplier embedded in OEM platforms via high switching costs.
APTV.reason: 17% FCF yield and 7.1x NTM P/E against guided EPS more than tripling is priced for a permanently weak auto cycle; cyclical and thin-margin, but statistically too cheap for the embedded, hard-to-replace content it supplies to advance without a closer look.

red_flags: Net debt/EBITDA 3.3x
Revenue barely growing (+2.3%)
T.one_line: Legacy integrated telecom carrier with fiber build-out; scale and spectrum moat but low organic growth.
T.reason: Fairly priced (10.1x NTM P/E, 5.8% FCF yield) with a well-covered 4.4% dividend, but negative forward EPS growth (likely a swollen prior-year comp) and mid-single-digit revenue growth don't clear the quality-or-growth bar; no disqualifying flag, just unremarkable.

red_flags: Negative book equity from aggressive buybacks (leverage-driven ROE not shown)
Consumer auto-parts spending sensitive to used-car age cycle turning
AZO.one_line: Auto-parts retailer with dense store/commercial-delivery network; repair-not-replace demand is recession-resistant.
AZO.reason: Guided EPS growth of 34% at 16.7x NTM P/E is cheap on a PEG basis, and the business model (DIY plus fast-growing commercial) is durable; the poor statistical model rank (479) looks like exactly the kind of screen-hiding-a-good-business case this triage is meant to catch, so it should get a full look despite the weak year of momentum (-30%).

red_flags: Documented related-party dealings with DriveTime (warranty commission income) and aggressive loan-sale/no-loss-reserve accounting, per Hindenburg report and company's own filings
Executive Chairman has a prior felony bank-fraud conviction (disclosed historical fact)
Q2 2026 FY guidance cut disappointed Wall Street despite record results (stock fell >20%)
FCF yield only 0.6% despite reported profitability
CVNA.one_line: Online used-car retailer with vertically integrated logistics; rapid growth but aggressive accounting practices.
CVNA.reason: Real revenue growth (+52%) is offset by weak cash conversion, real (not just alleged) related-party arrangements, and a guidance cut that signals deceleration; at 31x NTM P/E this is priced for perfection it hasn't delivered, so pass rather than advance.

red_flags: Net debt/EBITDA 4.4x, elevated further by pending Cox Communications merger
Revenue declining (-1.7%), broadband share pressure from fixed wireless (T-Mobile/Verizon) and fiber overbuilders
Secular video cord-cutting
CHTR.one_line: Cable/broadband operator (Spectrum) merging with Cox; deeply cheap on cash flow but structurally challenged.
CHTR.reason: 2.7x NTM P/E and 15% FCF yield reflect real secular decline and heavy leverage rather than pure mispricing; the Cox merger adds integration and balance-sheet risk on top. Cheap but not clearing the quality/growth bar, so not advanced.

red_flags: Broadband subscriber growth saturating; cable-video secular decline continues
Net debt/EBITDA 2.4x
CMCSA.one_line: Diversified media/broadband: Comcast cable plus NBCUniversal theme parks and Peacock, post-Versant cable-network spinoff.
CMCSA.reason: 16.3% FCF yield, 6.2x NTM P/E and a 6% dividend for a business with real diversification (parks/Epic Universe, content) beyond declining video; already flagged 'attractive' by the v1 model and this triage agrees.

red_flags: Negative margin (-38.7%), negative ROE, negative FCF and net debt/EBITDA of 8.6x on the standalone legacy business
Core wireless/pay-TV (DISH/Boost) business in structural decline
ECHO.one_line: Legacy DISH/Boost wireless and pay-TV operator that just monetized its spectrum in a ~$40bn sale to AT&T and SpaceX.
ECHO.reason: The FCC approved EchoStar's ~$40bn spectrum sales to AT&T ($23bn) and SpaceX ($17bn cash+stock) in May 2026, which should transform the balance sheet shown in this data card (which reflects the pre-close legacy operating business); this is a special-situation/asset-value story, not a quality-or-growth compounder, so it doesn't fit this framework's advance criteria despite the transformative cash event -- worth flagging separately as event-driven rather than fundamental.

red_flags: Negative margin, negative ROE, negative FCF
~$4-5bn/yr EV (Model e) losses continuing through at least 2029 per management
Dealer class-action alleging systematic warranty-reimbursement shortfalls; elevated recall/warranty costs
F.one_line: Legacy Detroit automaker; profitable core ICE/truck franchise offset by heavy EV losses and warranty costs.
F.reason: 6.6x NTM P/E looks cheap but reflects real, ongoing EV losses, recall costs and thin overall profitability; no clear catalyst to close the gap, so not advanced.

red_flags: Dual-class share structure entrenches Murdoch family control (governance)
Revenue jump partly reflects cyclical political ad spend, not all organic
FOXA.one_line: Fox News, Fox Sports and Tubi; must-carry cable news/live-sports content less exposed to streaming disruption.
FOXA.reason: 10.7x NTM P/E with low leverage (0.9x) and clean FCF for a business with real pricing power in live sports/news; governance concentration is a real but not disqualifying flag.

red_flags: Dual-class share structure entrenches Murdoch family control (governance)
Revenue jump partly reflects cyclical political ad spend, not all organic
FOX.one_line: Class B shares of Fox Corp (Fox News/Fox Sports/Tubi); same business and thesis as FOXA, no vote.
FOX.reason: Same underlying business as FOXA at a slightly cheaper multiple (9.6x NTM P/E); low leverage and real content moat support advancing alongside the A shares.

red_flags: Net debt/EBITDA 6.3x is inflated by normal GM Financial captive-finance leverage, not industrial debt
EV segment still losing money, though losses narrowing
Tariff policy remains a swing factor despite recent relief
GM.one_line: Detroit automaker with record NA truck/SUV profits, narrowing EV losses and easing tariff costs.
GM.reason: 5.6x NTM P/E and 29% FCF yield after two 2026 guidance raises (tariff relief post-Supreme Court ruling, EV losses shrinking) look too cheap for the improving earnings trajectory; the inherited v1 'excessive' verdict looks stale given fresh guidance raises and is rejected here pending full diligence, which should reconcile it against the still-real cyclicality and EV-transition risk.

red_flags: April 2026 jury verdict found Live Nation/Ticketmaster liable on every antitrust count (illegal monopolization, illegal tying); damages/remedies phase ongoing, structural remedies (e.g., Ticketmaster divestiture) not ruled out
GAAP margin near zero (0.5%)
LYV.one_line: Concert promoter and Ticketmaster owner; dominant live-events position now under an adverse antitrust verdict.
LYV.reason: 134.7x NTM P/E on a company that just lost an antitrust jury trial to 33 states plus DC, with remedies (potentially including divestiture) still to be decided, is priced for zero legal risk; disqualifying litigation overhang plus rich valuation means pass.

red_flags: Revenue declining (-4.3%) and forward EPS guided down (-29%)
Intensifying competition from Alo Yoga, Vuori, Athleta eroding pricing power
Tariff cost headwinds
LULU.one_line: Premium athleisure brand losing share and pricing power to fast-growing challenger brands in its core category.
LULU.reason: Cheap trailing P/E (8.3x) is a value trap signal, not an opportunity: forward earnings are expected to fall further and street upside is only 3.6%, confirming the market already sees limited recovery from here.

red_flags: Password-sharing/ad-tier monetization tailwinds are largely realized already; next leg of growth needs live sports/content execution
NFLX.one_line: Global streaming leader with unmatched content scale, algorithm and now profitable ad tier.
NFLX.reason: 13% revenue growth, 28% margins, 49.5% ROE and 19x NTM P/E for 20% EPS growth is an attractive PEG for the category leader; disciplined capital allocation shown by walking away from the WBD bidding war in Feb 2026 rather than overpaying.

red_flags: Dual-class share structure entrenches Murdoch family control (governance)
NWSA.one_line: Dow Jones/WSJ, HarperCollins and Move (realtor.com); real digital data/subscription moats inside a legacy publisher.
NWSA.reason: 45% guided EPS growth at ~21x NTM P/E is an attractive PEG for a diversified media/data business with genuine digital moats (Dow Jones data/risk products, Move real-estate listings); governance concentration flagged but not disqualifying.

red_flags: Dual-class share structure entrenches Murdoch family control (governance)
NWS.one_line: Voting Class B shares of News Corp; same business and thesis as NWSA at a modest premium for voting rights.
NWS.reason: Identical underlying business case to NWSA; advanced alongside it.

red_flags: China revenue still down double digits (~-20% guided for FQ4)
~$1.5bn annual tariff headwind through FY2027 Q1
Turnaround has already taken longer than management first expected
NKE.one_line: Global sportswear leader mid-turnaround under CEO Elliott Hill; running category re-accelerating, China still weak.
NKE.reason: Stock down >50% from highs now yields 4.5%; management guided gross margin to inflect positively starting FY2027 Q2 with five straight quarters of double-digit running growth already booked, so the brand's core strength looks intact even though the recovery is visibly slower than promised.

red_flags: Merger-integration risk from the 2025-2026 combination with Interpublic Group (largest ad-holding-company merger)
Secular threat from AI-driven ad creation/targeting disintermediating traditional agencies
OMC.one_line: Global advertising/marketing holding company that just merged with Interpublic Group to become the industry's largest.
OMC.reason: The extreme trailing P/E (205.8x) and 3,074% EPS-growth figure are merger-accounting noise, not the real story; normalized NTM P/E of 6.7x with 19.6% FCF yield is cheap if IPG integration goes reasonably well, but integration and AI-disruption risk both need real diligence.

red_flags: Pending $110bn all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery still faces multi-state antitrust litigation (trial set March 2027) and a WGA lawsuit
Negative net margin currently; elevated leverage (4.4x net debt/EBITDA) before the WBD deal even closes
Editorial-independence concerns raised over CBS News changes
PSKY.one_line: Newly merged Paramount/Skydance (CBS, Paramount Pictures, Paramount+) now attempting a leveraged, litigation-contested buyout of WBD.
PSKY.reason: Reported multiples (332x trailing P/E, near-158% FCF yield) look like data artifacts of the merger and financing structure rather than real per-share economics; with negative margins, real leverage and an unresolved antitrust trial hanging over the signature strategic move, this is too binary/uncertain to call cheap or call a quality-or-growth story right now.

red_flags: Meaningful reliance on Google search-referral traffic; AI answer engines (Overviews) could structurally reduce visits even as revenue currently grows fast
AI data-licensing ('Other revenue') growing slower (+24%) than the core ad business, the segment the market treats as its AI story
RDDT.one_line: Community-driven discussion platform monetizing ads plus AI/data licensing on a decade of unique human content.
RDDT.reason: Q2 2026: revenue +61% for an 8th straight quarter, DAU +18% to 130.3M, 31% net margin, net cash balance sheet, at just 22.6x NTM P/E; traffic-mix/search-dependency risk is real and caused the recent -36% momentum swing, so worth a full quality-of-growth diligence pass rather than dismissing on price alone.

red_flags: None disqualifying; valuation simply looks full for the growth rate on offer
ROST.one_line: Off-price apparel retailer (Ross/dd's Discounts) with strong buying-scale moat and best-in-class ROE.
ROST.reason: 42.6% ROE and low leverage confirm real quality, but 26.8x NTM P/E for only ~8% forward EPS growth (PEG >3x) with street upside of just 14% supports the inherited v1 'excessive' verdict; agree with it and pass for now.

red_flags: Net debt/EBITDA 3.4x
Fiber/fixed-wireless buildout (Metronet/Lumos JVs) requires sustained capex execution
TMUS.one_line: Leading 5G wireless carrier expanding into fixed-wireless broadband and fiber; best network, still taking share.
TMUS.reason: Guided 51% forward EPS growth at 12.6x NTM P/E with 47.6% street upside is a rare combination of real subscriber-growth momentum and a reasonable price, despite the stock being down 23% over the past year.

red_flags: Single-title dependency: near-term earnings inflection hinges almost entirely on GTA VI execution
Franchise has already slipped twice (May 2026 -> Nov 19, 2026); further slippage or a rocky launch (technical issues at this scale) is a real risk
Currently GAAP-unprofitable (negative margin/ROE) ahead of launch
TTWO.one_line: Rockstar Games' owner; GTA VI, the industry's most-anticipated release, is now reaffirmed for November 19, 2026.
TTWO.reason: Management has repeatedly reaffirmed the Nov 19, 2026 date (including in the latest earnings release) after pre-orders opened in June, which de-risks the single biggest catalyst in the video-game industry this decade; 57x NTM P/E already prices in a successful launch, so this is fairly rather than cheaply priced, but the growth inflection and franchise quality (200M+ lifetime GTA V units) warrant full diligence on launch economics.

red_flags: 180x NTM P/E and 338x trailing P/E versus a 3.7% auto gross margin and 4.7% ROE -- valuation is entirely dependent on unproven robotaxi/FSD/Optimus bets, not the current auto business
Street upside of only 6.6% signals even bullish sell-side targets are barely above the current price
TSLA.one_line: EV/energy/robotics company whose current valuation prices in flawless execution of still-speculative autonomy and robotics bets.
TSLA.reason: Headline 97.5% forward EPS growth is off a depressed, price-cut-driven base and doesn't come close to justifying a price this disconnected from current auto-segment economics (thin margins, low ROE, near-zero FCF yield); price versus plausible growth fails badly.

red_flags: None disqualifying
TJX.one_line: TJ Maxx/Marshalls/HomeGoods off-price retailer; treasure-hunt buying model with exceptional, consistent returns.
TJX.reason: 62.2% ROE and 30.6% street upside for a proven, resilient compounder justify paying a full 23x NTM P/E even at only high-single-digit forward EPS growth; quality alone clears the bar here.

red_flags: Still-thin reported margin (4.3%) while integrating WWE/UFC and ramping new media-rights economics
Net debt/EBITDA 2.7x
TKO.one_line: WWE plus UFC under one roof; irreplaceable live combat-sports/entertainment IP with major new media-rights deals.
TKO.reason: 64% guided EPS growth (WWE's move to Netflix, renewed UFC media rights) at 37.7x NTM P/E is a favorable PEG for content with genuine scarcity value and repeat pricing power at each rights renewal.

red_flags: Net debt/EBITDA 3.8x
Revenue essentially flat (-0.7%); forward EPS growth driven by cost-cutting/restructuring more than organic growth
VZ.one_line: Legacy wireless/fiber telecom incumbent mid-turnaround under new CEO-led cost program; high, well-covered dividend.
VZ.reason: 9x NTM P/E, 8.9% FCF yield and a 5.9% dividend make this statistically cheap (v1 already flags it 'attractive'), but quality and growth are both middling (mature, leveraged, restructuring-driven rather than demand-driven growth), so it doesn't clear the quality-or-growth bar here even though it is a reasonable watchlist name for income.

red_flags: ESPN direct-to-consumer streaming (launched Aug 2025) still ramping and unproven at scale
Linear TV secular decline continues to weigh on the cable segment
DIS.one_line: Best-in-class IP portfolio (Marvel, Star Wars, Pixar, ESPN, Parks) with streaming now sustainably profitable.
DIS.reason: 54% guided EPS growth (streaming profitability inflection plus ESPN DTC ramp and steady Parks growth) at 14.2x NTM P/E is an attractive PEG for a diversified content leader with few true peers.

red_flags: Being acquired by Paramount Skydance for $31/share cash; stock at $30.86 is already priced at the deal value (street upside -2.2%)
Deal still subject to state antitrust litigation (trial scheduled March 2027) and a stipulation not to close before June 2027 or trial resolution, though California settled Sept 21, 2026
Standalone business shows negative margin/ROE and declining revenue (-11.2%)
WBD.one_line: HBO/Warner Bros. studio and networks, now a merger-arbitrage situation pending a contested $110bn Paramount Skydance buyout.
WBD.reason: This is a binary risk-arb situation, not a fundamental quality/growth thesis: upside is capped near the deal price while downside risk comes from litigation delay or deal break, so it doesn't fit this framework's advance criteria and is better tracked as a special situation.
